RESULT: [P1] Task snapshots exceed the task-record reader limit and strand otherwise supported workspaces. skills/peer-coworkers/scripts/records.py:27-33 caps task.json at 4 MiB, while tasks.py:241-243 saves both baseline and collected_snapshot without enforcing that cap. Reproduced with 10,000 empty untracked file-00000.txt through file-09999.txt (well below snapshot defaults of 50,000 files/256 MiB): prepare writes a readable 2,730,931-byte task.json; collect succeeds and writes 5,461,663 bytes; the next read_json(task.json) raises ToolError: JSON must be a bounded regular file. Every subsequent CLI action, including accept and close, reads through this cap at cowork.py:109, so the run becomes unusable and any live lease cannot be normally released. Larger permitted workspaces fail immediately after prepare. Align bounded record storage/read limits with configurable snapshot capacity, or store snapshots separately with appropriate bounds, and test prepare/collect/reload/accept at realistic file counts.

[P1] Question observation clears the cancellation latch and allows a second Escape. skills/peer-coworkers/scripts/observation.py:62-64 unconditionally changes state to awaiting_reply, including when wait begins in cancelling. interactions.py:57-63 decides whether to send Escape solely from that state. Trigger: an awaiting_reply task still has valid current-round question.json; cancel sends Escape but cannot confirm stopping and leaves cancelling; wait reads the existing question and persists awaiting_reply; a subsequent cancel sends Escape again. This violates the explicit single-attempt cancellation requirement and can act on a later UI state. Preserve cancelling during question observation and/or bind cancellation delivery to a persistent intervention marker independent of mutable task state.
